source.title_on_document: Generative artificial intelligence models outperform students on divergent and convergent thinking assessments

supplement.where: Europe PMC metadata flags no supplement; Data availability: 'All relevant data supporting the findings of this study are included in the main manuscript. Raw data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.'

paper_design_summary: Forty-six McMaster University students completed the Alternate Uses Task (shoe, tire, pants; 3 minutes each) and 57 Remote Associates Test items (15 minutes) online without AI. The first author then ran 46 sessions each of ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini 2.0 with default settings, matching each AI session to one human's item order and number of ideas. AUT originality was scored by the Ocsai LLM scorer (ocsai1-4o, 1 to 5) and RAT items against an answer key; humans were compared with each model, and models with each other.

studies.label: Humans vs three GenAI chatbots on the AUT and RAT

participants.who: Undergraduate and graduate students aged 18 or older at McMaster University, any faculty, recruited by convenience snowball sampling; mean age 23.35 (SD 3.47); 28.26 percent not native English speakers. The AI side is 46 sessions per chatbot (ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.0), each matched to one human participant.
participants.quote: Human participants (n = 46) were recruited via convenience snowball sampling

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.0 (default parameters), tested February 16 to 23, 2025
ai_tool.how_used: The models produced output on their own as comparison 'participants'; no human used AI. Prompts fixed the number of AUT ideas to each matched human's fluency; only the title of each AI idea was scored.

task.description: Alternate Uses Task (shoe, tire, pants) scored for originality, and 57 Remote Associates Test items (convergent thinking) with normative accuracy of 30 to 80 percent
task.duration: Humans: 3 minutes per AUT item, 15 minutes for the RAT; no time limit for AI

outcomes.name: AUT median originality ('average' idea), per item
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Ocsai ocsai1-4o originality, 1 to 5; per-person median over ideas; Wilcoxon signed-rank on human-AI pairs matched for fluency. Contrast shown for ChatGPT-4o; DeepSeek median differences -0.625, -0.625, -0.500 and Gemini -0.750, -0.750, -0.550 (pants, shoe, tire), all p < 0.001 (Table 3). Co-primary objective.

contrasts.reported: Mean (SD) median originality, human vs ChatGPT: pants 2.96 (0.66) vs 3.77 (0.31); shoe 3.27 (0.63) vs 4.23 (0.26); tire 3.20 (0.48) vs 4.11 (0.30). Median difference (human minus AI), 95% CI: pants -0.800 (-1.000, -0.625), shoe -0.950 (-1.150, -0.750), tire -0.900 (-1.025, -0.750); p < 0.001 each
contrasts.locator: Results, Divergent thinking: originality of the 'average' idea; Tables 2 and 3

outcomes.name: AUT maximum originality ('best' idea), per item
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Ocsai ocsai1-4o originality, per-person maximum; Wilcoxon signed-rank on matched pairs. Contrast shown for ChatGPT-4o; DeepSeek -0.500 (p = 0.005), -0.550, -0.500 and Gemini -0.650, -0.600, -0.750 (pants, shoe, tire) (Table 3). Co-primary objective.

contrasts.reported: Mean (SD) max originality, human vs ChatGPT: pants 3.60 (0.55) vs 4.34 (0.24); shoe 4.04 (0.53) vs 4.47 (0.19); tire 3.69 (0.58) vs 4.47 (0.16). Median difference (human minus AI), 95% CI: pants -0.800 (-1.000, -0.750), shoe -0.550 (-0.750, -0.350), tire -1.000 (-1.000, -0.750); p < 0.001 each
contrasts.locator: Results, Divergent thinking: originality of the 'best' idea; Tables 2 and 3

outcomes.name: RAT number correct (of 57)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Scored against the Bowden and Jung-Beeman answer key, with spelling review; Student's t-tests of humans vs each model. DeepSeek 51.00 (SD 1.59) and Gemini 44.93 (SD 1.88), both p < 0.001 vs humans. Co-primary objective.

contrasts.reported: Human 19.13 (SD 9.96), range 2-42; ChatGPT 54.96 (SD 0.89), range 53-56; *** p < 0.001 (Student's t-test)

eligibility.reason: AI-generated output (ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.0 sessions) is compared with output from 46 students working without AI; no person receives AI help or is assigned to AI. Only task and item order were randomized (Methods, Procedure).

one_line_finding: All three chatbots beat 46 students on AUT originality and the RAT; for ChatGPT-4o the human-minus-AI median difference in median originality was -0.800 to -0.950 across items (p < 0.001), and RAT accuracy was 54.96 vs 19.13 of 57 (Tables 3 and 4).
